beats.text: To recap. Respiration oxidises food just as combustion oxidises a fuel, and the energy is conserved, partly as useful work and partly as heat. Food energy is estimated with factors of sixteen, seventeen and thirty-seven kilojoules per gram. Keep units attached when scaling, and always state the basis of a comparison.
Closing recall. How much energy do twenty grams of fat provide, using the food factor?
Twenty grams times thirty-seven kilojoules per gram is seven hundred and forty kilojoules. Next episode, we return to fuels and balance combustion equations, including incomplete combustion.
